title: Guitar
intro: These pages are lessons to work through with a guitar in your hands. Each one tells you where to put your fingers, what to play and what to listen for, with a fretboard you can play and step through. The theory comes from the piano-based Music Theory topic; here it is put under your fingers.

items: Have your guitar tuned and a pick (or your fingers) ready. Keep this page beside you on a tablet, laptop or phone.
Every lesson has numbered steps. Do each one on the guitar before reading on.

Every fretboard has a ▶ button for each example, plus ◀ Step and Step ▶ to go one chord or note at a time; the frets you need stay lit until you press Step again. Use Play all to hear the whole thing. Turn the sound off in the header if you only want to see the frets.
Fretboards are drawn as you look down at the neck while playing: the thinnest string (high e) is at the top, as in tab, and fret numbers increase to the right.
Each lesson ends with a practice routine (10 to 15 minutes) and a few questions to check yourself; the answers are hidden until you open them.
Lesson 1: Tuning, Tab and Chord Diagrams (#/arts/guitar/tuning-and-tab): tune the guitar, and read tab and chord diagrams.
Lesson 2: First Notes, First Chords (#/arts/guitar/technique): how to hold, fret, pick and strum, and your first chord change.
Lesson 3: The Notes on the Fretboard (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/fretboard): learn where every note is, starting with strings 6 and 5.
Roots (#/arts/music-theory/chords/roots): what the root of a chord is, and how to find it on the guitar (a short page in Music Theory with a guitar section).
Lesson 4: Intervals as Shapes (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/intervals-and-shapes): the distances between notes as fixed fingerings.
Lesson 5: Chords: Open, Barre, Power and Beyond (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/chord-voicings): building chords from roots and intervals.
Lesson 6: Scales (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/scales): the pentatonic box and the major scale in one position.
Lesson 7: The CAGED System (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/caged): five shapes that map every chord across the neck.
Lesson 8: Playing Progressions (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/harmony-and-progressions): chords in a key, the capo, and the progressions songs are made of.
Lesson 9: Soloing over Chords (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/soloing): arpeggios, target notes and bends.
Summary and Reference (#/arts/guitar/guitar-theory/summary): everything on one page, for looking things up.
Headstock with the tuning pegs; the nut (a slotted bar, 'fret 0'); the neck with its frets (metal strips; each is one semitone); the body; the bridge and saddle where the strings end.
Dots on the neck mark frets 3, 5, 7, 9, 12 (two dots), 15 and 17: they help you find your place.
Strings are numbered from the thinnest: string 1 is high E, string 6 is low E. In standard tuning they are, low to high: E A D G B E.

blocks.text: Frets get closer together up the neck because each one shortens the string by the same ratio, $2^{-1/12}$, raising the pitch by one equal-tempered semitone; the 12th fret is exactly halfway along the string, an octave up.
